title: Weekly pilot — seqlen prioritization & first-token latency huddle
next_steps: Redwood to run 2 new microburst experiments using sequence-length gated kernels by 2026-03-03
Customer to share 48-hour tail-latency traces and representative prompt set by 2026-03-01
Schedule side-by-side hosted vs dedicated 1k requests benchmark with streaming enabled (AE/SE owns scheduling)
action_items: Priya Shah — set up kernel gating experiment (quantized path vs float) and share perf sheet — due 2026-03-03
Miguel Ortega — export p50/p95/p99 TTFT and stream handshake traces for last 2 days — due 2026-03-01

summary: Mid-poc sync focused on reducing time-to-first-token and stabilizing streaming handshake for varied sequence lengths. Agreed to run kernel gating experiments and to exchange traces and prompt sets. Discussed viable tradeoffs between dedicated and hosted routes for their compliance needs.
topics: streaming handshake failures during microburst traffic
KV/prefix cache behavior with doc-heavy prompts
short-term pilot next steps and security ask
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-27 10:30 PT — 48 minutes. Attendees: James Miller (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Logan Reyes (Redwood SRE), Sara Collins (Aurelia Head of ML), Miguel Ortega (Platform Eng), Tina Zhao (Infra Lead).

[00:00] James Miller: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um let's do a quick agenda — TTFT numbers, streaming handshakes, sequence-length kernel gating, and then action items. Sara, Miguel, anything to add?

[00:22] Sara Collins: No, that's perfect. We're mainly worried about first-token regressions we saw after the quantization change last week. p95 jumped and, um, we've seen some handshake timeouts on stream.

[00:38] Priya Shah: Right, thanks Sara. Quick call out: we pushed a conservative quantized kernel last Tuesday which improved throughput but we saw a p95 bump in TTFT for short prompts. We suspect the kernel selection path adds a tiny decision overhead that compounds in microburst patterns.

[01:05] Miguel Ortega: Just to give context — our workload is a lot of short clinical note completions, avg seqlen ~ 28 tokens, but there are spikes where a long patient history comes in and sequences hit 1.2k. The mixed profile seems to confuse the runtime.

[01:28] Logan Reyes: That matches what our profiler showed: the runtime was switching paths at inference time when it detected longer tail sequences which caused KV reallocation and small GC-ish pauses. Probably not GC but memory reshuffle.

[01:45] Tina Zhao: Also we run inside a VPC with strict egress rules, so fallback to hosted variants is trickier. We have to keep everything within the private deployment; that's why dedicated/dedicated-like predictable latency is important to us.

[02:04] James Miller: Understood. Two immediate levers: 1) Sequence-length gated kernel selection — pick kernel variant at request admission based on expected effective seqlen and stick to it for the request, avoid mid-request switching. 2) Streaming handshake tuning — make the handshake lighter and overlap more with model warmup.

[02:32] Priya Shah: We ran a quick offline test: when we pin the kernel at admission for seqlen bucket <64 we reduced TTFT p95 by ~18% on our dev rig. But in production microburst arrivals that interleave short and long requests cause queuing oddities.

[02:52] Sara Collins: I want to understand the tradeoffs — does pinning at admission risk suboptimal kernel for long tail sequences? Like if a request is mis-categorized initially.

[03:08] Priya Shah: Good question. Mitigation: admission uses a cheap seqlen estimate from the prompt prefix (we already compute prompt tokenization upstream). For borderline cases we set a short guard-band and use a hybrid KV layout that supports both without full reallocation. It's slightly more memory but much cheaper than a mid-request swap.

[03:37] Miguel Ortega: Any numbers on memory overhead? We have tight limits on GPU memory for our Dedicated node pools.

[03:46] Priya Shah: Roughly +4–6% VRAM on average for hybrid path on our 32GB-ish templates. We can run a targeted test against your instance sizes to confirm.

[04:00] James Miller: Actionable: Priya will run kernel gating tests with quantized vs float variants using Aurelia's sample prompts. We'll include a mem profile.

[04:10] Miguel Ortega: On streaming: our infra team saw ~15% of streams fail the initial handshake under bursts; the client then retries which doubles latency. Is there a way to make the handshake idempotent or faster?

[04:27] Logan Reyes: We have two ideas — reduce the handshake RTT by moving part of the negotiation to a pre-warm path (staged handshake) and accept optimistic streaming frames with a soft-accept fallback. Both require some client change but minimal.

[04:48] Tina Zhao: Client changes are ok as long as they don't require broad SDK churn. We use a custom wrapper around the SDK currently.

[04:58] Priya Shah: For the optimistic frames approach we can gate it behind a 'pilot' flag; Redwood's hosted SDK can opt-in and your wrapper can follow. That would reduce time-to-first-byte for streaming by letting the model start sending tokens while finalizing some non-critical headers.

[05:20] Sara Collins: That sounds promising — what's the failure mode? If the handshake fails after we've started sending token frames do we lose correctness?

[05:30] Logan Reyes: We build in an idempotent token ACK. If the handshake ultimately fails the client drops frames and retries the request; worst case you have one extra roundtrip but we avoid the initial full timeout. In practice it's cut down p99 from 1.8s to 1.2s in our internal tests.

[05:52] Miguel Ortega: Can you replicate that in our environment where we have the VPC NAT throttle? Those NAT transients seem to exacerbate handshake timeouts.

[06:03] James Miller: Yes — we'll include the VPC egress conditions in the bench. Miguel — please share a short window of your NAT metrics and we'll replay similar conditions in the pilot.

[06:13] Miguel Ortega: Sure, will do.

[06:18] Sara Collins: One other thing: we noticed TTFT regressions correlate with KV cache misses when the system switches to longer sequences; our long prompts flush prefix cache more often. Is there a recommended caching policy?

[06:34] Priya Shah: For doc-heavy prompts we recommend an LRU prefix cache with size tuned by observed prefix reuse. Also adaptive prefix caching where repeated patient IDs or templates are pinned for a short TTL — that reduced cache churn in a healthcare pilot we did last quarter.

[06:55] Tina Zhao: That sounds good, but pinned TTLs sound like extra state — how do you surface that for our infra team?

[07:03] Priya Shah: We can expose a small telemetry endpoint and a config flag in the control plane. We'll provide a suggested starting config and the Redwood Console will show pin hit rates.

[07:18] James Miller: Let's walk through today's benchmark results quickly — Priya?

[07:23] Priya Shah: I shared a short perf doc earlier. TL;DR: baseline hosted config — p50 TTFT 120ms, p95 430ms, p99 980ms; after quantized kernel swap we saw p50 drop to 95ms but p95 rose to 520ms and p99 to 1.05s. When we pinned small seqlen kernel at admission we saw p95 340ms and p99 900ms, so improved tail.

[08:00] Miguel Ortega: So quantization improved median but hurt tail. Any visibility into why p99 increased slightly?

[08:10] Priya Shah: The heavier kernel selection logic plus occasional path switches caused transient queueing. Also memory defragmentation during path swap — small but visible in tails. Pinning solves the path switch.

[08:28] Sara Collins: Are these numbers from Redwood's hosted infra or a dedicated sim?

[08:34] Priya Shah: These are run on hosted dev cluster with similar GPU types but without your VPC constraints. We need to run the dedicated/pilot bench against your Dedicated node to be accurate.

[08:47] Tina Zhao: We also need to compare idle vs cold-start behavior; some of our requests coincide with cold cache after nightly batch jobs which creates longer tails.

[08:58] Logan Reyes: We can simulate cold-start by clearing KV caches between runs in the bench. We'll add that axis.

[09:08] Sara Collins: Anything we should be cautious about from the security side? You mentioned a small telemetry endpoint — must be within our VPC and audit logged.

[09:17] James Miller: Absolutely. We'll deliver a minimal network diagram and specify that telemetry is optional and can be routed to your KMS-backed secure endpoint. We'll include SOC2 attestations and audit log options.

[09:30] Miguel Ortega: Could you also include the per-token cost delta for the hybrid gating? We need to present cost vs latency tradeoff to procurement.

[09:40] Priya Shah: We'll include a unit economics table — expected tokens/sec delta, resource utilization, and estimated $/1M tokens for each path.

[09:50] Tina Zhao: On timeline — what's realistic for the kernel gating experiment and the streaming optimistic frames trial?

[09:58] James Miller: Proposal: kernel gating experiments by 2026-03-03 with results shared; streaming optimistic frames prototype for SDK by 2026-03-08, then a short pilot run in your staging environment.

[10:12] Sara Collins: Works for us.

[10:16] James Miller: Great. Recap of action items: Priya runs kernel gating tests and includes memory profile; Miguel shares traces and NAT metrics; James sends security + pricing; Logan adds cold-start axis to benches. We'll reconvene next Friday same time.

[10:32] Miguel Ortega: Quick question — did we decide on hosted vs dedicated for the pilot?

[10:37] James Miller: We left that open — short term we'll run dual runs: hosted baseline and dedicated pilot run to compare. Given your VPC needs likely dedicated will win, but the bench will confirm.

[10:49] Sara Collins: Also please include a simple A/B prompt set where we instrument prompt prefixes so we can see where prefix pins help.

[10:58] Priya Shah: Will do.

[11:02] James Miller: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with notes and scheduling stuff. End.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts: 'KV cache' transcribed as 'K-V cash' in some utterances. Speaker overlap at 04:50 and 09:50 produced minor attribution errors.
